Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Assessment summary (from transcript):
  - Acute onset (~15 minutes) of symptoms after wasp sting: shallow breathing, chest tightness, perioral tingling, and blotchy rash.
  - No reported throat swelling or collapse; patient conversant and ambulatory at time of call.
  - Patient has antihistamines at home; allergic to penicillin; history of eczema.
  - Clinician judged potential for anaphylaxis and advised urgent ambulance and administration of antihistamine while awaiting transfer.
- DDx integration (only items consistent with transcript):
  - IgE‑mediated anaphylaxis due to wasp sting — High likelihood (supported by rapid onset after sting, respiratory symptoms, perioral paresthesia, and new rash). Clinician acted accordingly (urgent ambulance recommended).
  - Generalized allergic reaction / large local cutaneous reaction — Moderate likelihood (blotchy rash and only mild respiratory symptoms currently).
  - Asthma/reactive airways exacerbation and acute anxiety/panic reaction — Lower likelihood but considered in DDx; less supported by history (no prior asthma, presence of rash favors allergic cause).
- Conflicts/uncertainties:
  - No direct contradictions between transcript and DDx; both prioritize anaphylaxis as likely. Vital signs and objective exam findings are not recorded and limit definitive assessment.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- 1) IgE‑mediated anaphylaxis due to wasp sting — High likelihood
  - Justification: Rapid onset (~15 minutes) after sting, respiratory symptoms (shallow breathing/chest tightness), perioral tingling, and new blotchy rash. Clinician advised ambulance and antihistamine.
- 2) Generalized allergic reaction / large local cutaneous reaction — Moderate likelihood
  - Justification: Presence of urticarial/blotchy rash and only mild respiratory symptoms at presentation; could represent non‑anaphylactic systemic cutaneous reaction or large local reaction with anxiety‑related dyspnea.
- 3) Asthma/reactive airways exacerbation (triggered by allergen) — Low likelihood
  - Justification: Acute chest tightness could reflect bronchospasm but no prior asthma history or documented wheeze; concurrent rash and lip tingling favor systemic allergic reaction.
- (DDx also listed mast cell disorder and anxiety/panic as possibilities — noted in DDx but lower likelihood given current presentation.)
